laterChanges: Georgia enacted a 2026 Property Tax Relief Grant providing an $18,000 assessed-value reduction to qualifying homesteads; it is not a 2025 credit.
name: Georgia
overview: Georgia combines statewide minimum homestead exemptions with locally adopted exemptions.

programs.name: State-law homestead exemptions
programs.ageRule: General homeowner exemption, with additional age-based options.
programs.incomeDefinition: Senior exemptions use specially defined prior-year income; some retirement income excluded.
programs.incomeLimits: The age-65 county exemption uses a $10,000 claimant/spouse income limit.
programs.maximumBenefit: General $2,000 assessed-value exemption; additional senior and local exemptions differ.
programs.formulaSummary: Reduces taxable assessed value for specified county/school levies.
programs.application: Apply through county tax officials by applicable homestead deadline.
eligibilityNotes: Local exemptions may be more generous than the state-law minimum.

programs.name: Real estate taxes in Georgia itemized deductions
programs.ageRule: No age test on this deduction.
programs.incomeDefinition: Georgia starts with itemized deductions used on the federal return. Federal modified adjusted gross income can limit deductible state and local taxes.
programs.incomeLimits: Georgia imposes no separate income limit on this component. Federal adjusted gross income can affect the combined federal tax deduction.
programs.maximumBenefit: The amount of eligible real estate taxes that fits within the combined state and local tax limits. Georgia adds back the portion of the federal deduction that exceeds $10,000, or $5,000 for married taxpayers filing separately.
programs.formulaSummary: Taxpayers who itemize on their federal return use federal itemized deductions in Georgia, subject to state adjustments. Eligible property taxes are included in those deductions.
programs.application: Attach federal Schedule A to Georgia Form 500 and complete lines 12a through 12c. Follow the instructions for adjustments to your federal amounts.
eligibilityNotes: Use the federal qualified real estate tax amount from Schedule A line 5b.
interactions: Georgia follows the taxpayer’s federal choice of standard or itemized deductions. The state cap on the combined tax deduction may be lower than the federal cap.
programs.programYear: 2025 Georgia income tax return and 2025 federal Schedule A.

sources.title: 2025 Georgia IT-511 instructions and Form 500 lines 11–12c

researchNotes: The listed 2025 program covers homestead exemptions. Periodic homeowner grants use their own tax years.
